text.content:
The @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.f6a3258d39874a5c]{Anarch Movement} occupies a middle ground between the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}'s insistence on social order and the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}'s embrace of individual liberty. Rather than a single ideology, the Movement is a spectrum of "political impulses" - loose, largely unspoken ideological leanings rather than formal, card-carrying factions. Anarchs rarely label themselves or one another this precisely (no one walks up to a comrade and asks "are you a Reformer?"), but the impulses below describe recognizable, recurring patterns of belief and behavior found across the Movement, from the Loyal Opposition still working from inside the Camarilla to the true "disloyal" anarchs who have broken with it entirely, plus a fringe of unaligned opportunists who get lumped in with the Cause whether they like it or not.

Most anarchs come to the Movement by choice, driven less by economic argument than by simple self-respect - a refusal to wait at the elders' table for scraps. A smaller number are "anarchs by accident,": vampires framed, outlawed or otherwise cast out who had nowhere else to go, some of whom never truly embrace the Cause and drift back to their old sect once their trouble passes, while others become the Movement's most loyal converts. Two especially rare accidental cases are Sabbat refugees (pack survivors who slip away when a weak or absent Vinculum fails to hold them, and who bring useful Disciplines and intelligence when they defect to the anarchs) and "enlightened" elders who genuinely renounce elder privilege and join the Cause, bringing centuries of boons and influence with them.

Stance: Loyal Opposition (within the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla})

Sympathizers are Camarilla loyalists, usually young elders, who wholeheartedly support the sect in theory but object to abuses common among its elders. They will back a just prince, but see him as "first among equals" who should be checked by a strong primogen council, and they sympathize with ancillae and neonates suffering under despotic rule. Sympathizers are not true anarchs and are openly contemptuous of anarch violence, which they see as poorly argued and self-defeating; they believe the system works fine when elders exercise power with wisdom and noblesse oblige. They operate almost entirely through quiet prestation, calling in favors to unseat an arrogant prince and install a more lenient successor, rarely allowing any visible link between themselves and the anarchs they occasionally benefit.

What It Means for a Character

A Sympathizer character is an insider, not a rebel - she works the Camarilla's own machinery of boons and influence to blunt elder abuses, and is quick to distance herself from anarchs who resort to open defiance. Other elders may see her as a useful, if occasionally inconvenient, voice for moderation; anarchs see her as a fair-weather ally at best.

Stance: Loyal Opposition (within the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla})

Reformers are loyalists, usually very young elders or older ancillae, who grudgingly support the Camarilla in theory but object to its outdated structure in practice. They chafe at concentrating so much power in a single prince and argue that true authority should rest in the primogen council; some even advocate that primogen and princes alike should be elected. Reformers insist they act in the sect's own best interest - the Camarilla must modernize or dissolve - and while they publicly distance themselves from self-avowed anarchs to avoid being tarred with the same brush, in private many tolerate or quietly support anarch activity so long as it doesn't go too far. Like Sympathizers, they work through prestation and connections, but are less shy about brokering "shady deals" when honest means fail.

What It Means for a Character

A Reformer character openly agitates for structural change from within Camarilla channels - electoral primogen, weakened princely authority - and risks being publicly labeled and disowned as an anarch if her efforts succeed too well. She occupies an uneasy space: too disruptive for the establishment, too compromised for true anarchs to fully trust.

Stance: Loyal Opposition (first impulse to openly wear the "anarch" label)

Constructionists are the first group to accept, however reluctantly, the label "anarch." Mostly ancillae who have lost faith in the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, they believe the sect is doomed to collapse under its own stagnation and want a viable alternative built and ready to take its place. They avoid open conflict, keep a low profile, and spend their time quietly recruiting and refining their theories rather than fighting; being older and comparatively well-established, they have too much to lose to risk it in violent rebellion. Most envision a loose confederation of independent city-states ruled by representative councils - functionally identical to what Reformers want, except Constructionists reject any unifying central authority (i.e., no Inner Circle, no justicars).

What It Means for a Character

A Constructionist character is a patient, evolutionary (not revolutionary) planner - she builds parallel institutions rather than tearing down existing ones, and defends herself only when directly threatened. She has real resources and standing, making her a valuable, if cautious, ally to more radical anarchs.

Stance: Disloyal Opposition (true anarch, outside @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} law)

Radicals are usually the Movement's youngest members - often mortal activists and firebrands who carried their politics into undeath - and its most idealistic. They believe the Camarilla teeters on the edge of collapse and dedicate themselves to pushing it over by any means necessary, favoring propaganda and nonviolent methods over direct force wherever possible; devotion to the struggle itself, not government or military action, is their paramount concern. Unlike Militants, Radicals take a "universalist" view: after liberating one city, they often move on to export revolution elsewhere rather than consolidating their hold, which produces the Movement's best political thinkers but its worst tacticians - Radicals frequently win the war but lose the peace.

What It Means for a Character

A Radical character is a gifted rabble-rouser and propagandist more invested in spreading the Cause than administering a single territory. She is a poor choice to run a city day-to-day, but invaluable at rallying new converts and destabilizing enemy domains.

Stance: Disloyal Opposition (true anarch, outside @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} law)

Militants, mostly neonates and young ancillae, are strident in their opposition to elder rule and believe - like Constructionists - that the Camarilla will self-destruct, but see no reason to wait for that collapse to happen on its own. "Militant" describes a level of devotion to direct action, not a requirement to use violence: what defines them is the conviction that decisive action, whatever form it takes, must fall outside the scope of Camarilla law. Militants favor independent, sovereign city-states that deal with each other as they choose rather than any larger confederation, and they defend their territory and communities with deadly force against elders who threaten them, unlike Constructionists who will typically cede ground rather than fight.

What It Means for a Character

A Militant character has drawn a hard line and expects - even welcomes - direct confrontation with elder power. She is a natural territory-holder and defender, distrustful of half-measures, and considers compromise with the Camarilla simply impossible.

Stance: Disloyal Opposition (true anarch, outside @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} law)

Hardliners are anarchs who have suffered greatly - at the hands of sires, sheriffs, scourges or princes - and are driven by rage rather than ideology. Like other anarchs they believe the Camarilla is on its last legs, but they lack the patience to wait for propagandists to win hearts and minds; they want their revolution now, and are willing to court violent confrontation on almost any terms, often more to prove devotion than to actually win. For most Hardliners the struggle isn't about building a better world - it's about making the elders suffer as they themselves have suffered, and revenge, not justice, is the true motive beneath whatever ideology they claim. They give little thought to complex politics or "what comes after," and aren't picky about allies, occasionally cooperating even with @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} packs if it means bringing down a hated elder.

What It Means for a Character

A Hardliner character is defined by a personal grievance against the establishment rather than a coherent political program. She is an effective, motivated fighter, but her willingness to work with anyone (even the Sabbat) to settle old scores makes her judgment suspect to more principled anarchs.

Stance: Anarch Fringe (not true anarchs, often mistaken for them)

Autarchs' only real political belief is that they don't do politics. They keep to themselves, manage their own affairs, avoid entanglement with other vampires, and can be genuinely offended at being called "anarchs" - they left the sects specifically to escape labels and cliques. At best they maintain strict neutrality and deal fairly, if distantly, with whoever they must; at worst they hold open contempt for the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} and Anarch Revolt alike. Some are young and hope to survive by staying uninvolved; others are old and powerful enough that mutual disregard has simply become the most convenient arrangement. When passing through a Camarilla domain, an autarch typically makes only a token appearance before the prince and disappears back into the city or countryside. Anarchs find autarchs hard to criticize (their independence is exactly what the Movement claims to want) but view their apathy as part of the problem, and neither side expects lasting support from the other.

What It Means for a Character

An Autarch character is a true loner who will cooperate with anarchs only for common cause or mutual defense, and bristles at being folded into the Movement's identity. She trades political influence for near-total independence.

Stance: Anarch Fringe (not true anarchs, often mistaken for them)

Mercenaries, like Autarchs, care nothing for sect or Cause, but unlike Autarchs they readily involve themselves in political conflicts - for a price. Some hold to a rough code of honor; most sell to the highest bidder, though nearly all avoid switching sides once hired, since doing so invites swift and lasting retaliation among the Kindred. Both elders and anarchs look down on mercenaries as social parasites while valuing their usefulness; pragmatic Militants and Radicals see nothing wrong with hiring them to bolster battlefield strength, while more idealistic anarchs insist that "liberation forces" should be volunteers only. Mercenaries themselves are indifferent to the debate - conflict is business, and business is good.

What It Means for a Character

A Mercenary character fights for coin, not conviction, and is a reliable hired blade exactly as long as the pay continues. She is tolerated more than trusted by anarchs and elders alike, prized for capability and viewed with suspicion for her lack of a cause.

Stance: Anarch Fringe (the Movement's black sheep)

Nihilists are almost without exception brutal misfits less than thirty years dead who resent any limit on their personal freedom and revel in their new powers with little or no concern for mortals; their "agenda," such as it is, amounts to "party, party, party." They are motivated by self-interest rather than ideology - many were criminals or troubled individuals as mortals - and though a minority within the Movement, their outrageous behavior draws the most attention, so much so that mainstream @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.fc464242d84d4e34]{Camarilla} vampires often assume all anarchs are Nihilists. As a result, Nihilists frequently find themselves fighting other anarchs (some of whom make a personal crusade of purging them from the ranks) as often as they fight princes, sheriffs or scourges. Those who survive more than a decade after the Embrace usually end up joining the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}; there is often little difference between a Nihilist gang and a Sabbat pack besides the absence of the Vaulderie.

What It Means for a Character

A Nihilist character feels no solidarity with the Cause and actively resists any restraint. She is a liability the Movement tolerates unevenly - useful muscle to some, a marked enemy to anarchs who see her as an embarrassment and a threat to the Movement's credibility.

vtmlarp.source: MET Mind's Eye Theatre Anarchs Guide
